question: Can joint-only reference targets for supporting stance feet restore a floor-upright body posture and remove the observed opposite-corner reach conflict without worsening stance losses or walking? The saved-input precheck does not answer the physical question.
controlled_change: Relative to V40, change composed position goals only for an active wave's currently contact-bearing stance feet. Use the existing all-four-leg support geometry at a floor-upright REFERENCE orientation and measured floor-relative torso height. All unselected goals retain V40's measured-pose geometry. Existing reference slew, absent-contact/full-rate selector, supported wave-rate fallback, gains and caps remain.
selector: current_wave.active AND current scheduled phase is an integer in 73..359 AND presence is explicitly true AND bears_support is explicitly true. Both joints share the same current selector. A contact-present but nonbearing foot is not selected. Missing, crossed, malformed or contradictory contact provenance must fail closed.
reference_geometry: Preserve authored horizontal-floor/frame provenance. In the existing anatomical vertical projection, the reference has forward_y=0, up_y=1 and side_y=0; all upright yaws share these projections. Use the measured floor-relative torso height, compiled geometry, existing nominal directions, knee fractions, per-joint limits and all four height constraints in the same feasible-plan/goal algebra. Do not overwrite the measured pose, synthesize an observation quaternion, or replace original contact truth. Reference-pose geometry is explicitly labeled as a controller target, not a measured pose or contact claim.
wave_comparison: Compute the current selector once from the real current wave and pre-command contacts. Hold that same selector for current and previous-wave goal evaluations, with one current measured height, one reference pose choice and one incoming reference-position vector. Do not turn a selector/frame switch into an alleged wave derivative. Previous-wave activation and positive dt requirements remain V40's.
rates_and_motor_formula: Apply V40 reference slew to the selected goals. With both waves active and dt>0, absent contacts retain clamp((bounded_target-incoming_reference)/dt) and other contacts retain clamp((bounded_target-bounded_comparison)/dt), using existing caps. Otherwise rate is zero. Motor velocity remains host sign -1 times clamp(8*(reference-measured_position)-0.65*measured_velocity+1.65*rate). Keep truthful saturation, speed/impulse slots and joint bounds.
memory_and_receipt: Distinct profile/policy/memory/receipt identities; no new dynamic state. Carry actual selected reference positions, previous time and the unchanged upstream wave snapshot. Add an optional V41-only upright_stance receipt exposing source step/time/capability/floor provenance, per-foot pre-command contact and current selector, explicitly labeled measured-pose baseline proposals, floor-upright reference proposals/plan, actual selected goals and the same-mask comparison choice. Existing actual target/rate/motor fields must reflect actual selected commands. Never label measured-pose baseline goals as actual selected goals when they differ; retain both explicitly for independent reconstruction. Absent optional fields must preserve older-policy serialized bytes.
preserve: V40 and all older policy/profile/DLL/output identities and all observed physical results.
Same-input V40 composed goals and final commands for every unselected limb with identical incoming reference memory; distinguish this from changed-memory replay.
V40 upstream wave snapshots, gait clocks, steering, contact/recontact/sync gates and dwell. Reference positions may differ as the intended controlled change; memory identity is distinct.
Zero-amplitude neutral goals, dt=0 initial reference hold, inactive/activation feedforward behavior and invalid-input safe refusal.
Existing joint bounds, speed and impulse caps, reference slew and servo gains; no fitted contact-count threshold or altered support predicate.
V20 recovery, stance V7, BW5R-B setup/prefix, original development schedule/evaluator and no-claim publication. No horizon or timeout extension is selected.
required_zero_world_checks: Real stateless and stateful exported interfaces on all 400 original V40 physical inputs, with chained actual candidate memory and exact input precision.
Independent reconstruction of measured and upright goal plans, selector/provenance, current-mask wave comparison, actual bounded references, selected rates and final motor velocities.
Separate one-command comparisons against V40 with identical incoming memory, covering all changed and unchanged commands; chain carry must not be misreported as same-memory equivalence.

Selector and runtime refusal checks covering phases 0/72/73/359, present/nonbearing/absent/contradictory contacts, initial/active/inactive waves, dt=0/positive, malformed geometry/floor/time/state and contact switching.
Synthetic upright-pose identity control and tilted-pose selection; no selected virtual pose may overwrite the actual measured observation.
Preserve all older-policy native output bytes and recovery fixtures. Keep the candidate component profile non-runnable until shared worker/adapter/motor-ledger/reader integration is verified.
Complete applicable safety gate before a distinct fresh bounded development diagnostic. The precheck selects no physical attempt.
risks_and_remaining_blockers: The upright all-four-leg geometry is nonempty on all 400 old inputs, not necessarily on a future trajectory and not proof of native contact or stable posture.
Old-input chained reference replay produces 168 speed-clamped commands versus V40's 85. One-command substitution produces 83; the latter must not hide chained cost.
Reference carry changes 102 currently unselected joint commands in the sketch; all 47 selector transitions are retained. Abrupt loss/restoration of contact can increase instability.

Some selected foot goals move upward at the fixed original torso. Desired body lowering assumes sustained anchoring; unilateral contact may instead lift a foot. Supporting-foot load transfer and delivered force remain unproved.

The old inputs include 131 two-contact, 175 three-contact and 94 four-contact commands. No data demonstrate physical behavior with zero or one supporting contact; synthetic refusal/bounds checks do not supply that evidence.
Rear-left's original 56 landing inputs and all original stance/relocation failures remain unchanged data. This proposal does not claim to explain or repair every failure.
Second complete planned cycles, commanded stop/cooldown, fresh paired commissioning and prospective acceptance remain required.
This is pose/contact-based SDK1 development, not real-time force-aware recovery, superiority, cross-engine equivalence, robustness or release authority.
